solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Evidence of sale about to be put by chair reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the words sound when said

blocks.note: a chair is a seat; spelt to match the sound

explanation.surface: A shop worker sets an item about to be sold beside a chair, as proof it was bought.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus SEAT gives RESEAT, which said aloud matches the answer: RE-CEIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the written slip that proves a purchase took place.

clue.text: Bit of excellent work in NY by top volunteers brought up for refinement

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its opening letter
in a down entry, brought up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: labour as spelt in American English
top is number one, written NO I
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Fine work in New York by leading volunteers is held up as polish.
explanation.walkthrough: NY signals the American spelling without the U. The reversal covers only the top and volunteers pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaboration is the process of developing something in greater detail, a refining of it.

clue.text: Catholic lecturer in Eastern part of church in Vatican City?

indicators.note: one thing in another is held inside it, so these letters are placed within

blocks.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A Catholic lecturer stands in the eastern part of a Vatican church.
explanation.walkthrough: Vatican City is a tiny state wholly surrounded by Rome; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is territory entirely surrounded by another state, which Vatican City is within Italy.

clue.text: Roman is misbehaving in confines of party avoiding excess

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting out of order, so these letters fall into a new order
in places one thing inside another, here inside the outer pair
the confines of a word are its boundaries, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Roman behaving badly at a party is kept within bounds and goes easy on the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme frugality, a refusal to spend more than is needed, so it avoids excess.

clue.text: Intellectual front anticipated by one in clutch?

indicators.note: to be anticipated by something is to have it come first, fixing the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a clutch is a set of eggs laid together
the head is the front, as of a queue

explanation.surface: Someone clever is beaten to the front by a person grabbing at things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clutch' suggests grasping, but here it is a nest of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Egghead is an informal, slightly mocking noun for a bookish, highly educated person.

clue.text: Former England cricket captain go up in grungier garb

indicators.note: in here means contained within the run of letters across the next words
in a down answer, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: An ex-England skipper climbs into scruffy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Greig captained England at cricket in the 1970s and later became a well-known commentator.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Greig was a South African-born all-rounder who led the England Test side.

clue.text: Sausage, not cold, close to oven? It's viewed distantly

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is taken out
the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken

blocks.note: chorizo is a spicy Spanish sausage

explanation.surface: A cooling sausage sits near the oven, glimpsed from across the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizon is the line where earth meets sky, always seen far off in the distance.

clue.text: Purpose concealed by claimant

indicators.note: something concealed by a word is tucked away inside its letters

blocks.note: letters from the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A claimant keeps the real motive under wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is a goal or intention, the same thing as a purpose.

clue.text: Actress with posh outfit certainly taken with old man, one successful in court?

blocks.note: OK as a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed actress arrives with an elderly man, someone who wins in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Novak Djokovic is the Serbian tennis player with a record haul of Grand Slam titles.

clue.text: A person came largely in order to get cheese

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the final letter of the word before is dropped
putting things in order means rearranging them, so the letters are sorted into a new sequence

blocks.note: the word with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: Someone arrived, mostly in good time, to pick up some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascarpone is a soft, creamy Italian cheese used in tiramisu.

clue.text: Sheep with soft fleece?

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A sheep with a soft woolly coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' sits naturally beside sheep as wool, but it is the verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramp is British slang for swindling someone, just as fleecing is overcharging or cheating them.

clue.text: Reproduction in main salon obscuring one new painting

indicators.note: a reproduction is something made again, so the letters are remade in a different arrangement
to obscure something is to hide it from view, so those letters disappear from the fodder

blocks.note: a single N, the abbreviation for new, which is removed

explanation.surface: A copy hung in the main gallery hides a newly acquired picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one N from MAIN SALON leaves eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mona Lisa is Leonardo da Vinci's portrait in the Louvre, an example of a painting.

clue.text: Fixed look by short lad in summerhouse

indicators.note: something short lacks its full length, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a gaze is a long steady look
a lad is a boy, here missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A boy stares fixedly at something while sitting in a garden house.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden building giving shade and a view, a kind of summerhouse.

clue.text: Boat lately at sea carrying Republican in fierce fight

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so these letters are jumbled
carrying means holding within, so one letter goes inside the rest

explanation.surface: A boat recently out at sea with a Republican aboard is the scene of a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle royal is a free-for-all fight involving many people, a fierce and noisy struggle.

clue.text: Sale a doc organised – medico's responsibility?

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange things, so these letters are put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor has arranged a sale, which seems an odd thing for them to be in charge of.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a caseload belongs to many professions; a doctor is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A caseload is the number of patients or cases a professional such as a doctor is handling.

clue.text: Signify poor grades obtained with regressive school

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: D and E are low marks
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Low marks were earned at a school that is going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to stand for or indicate, which is what signifying means.

clue.text: Extremely bad exercise by miserable specimen following son in river

indicators.note: in puts the group inside another word

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales
a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A poor swimmer exercising after his son in a river does very badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate can mean dire or extremely serious, as in a desperate situation that is extremely bad.

clue.text: Island stay's beginning in an unfriendly manner

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

blocks.note: an icy manner is cold and unwelcoming

explanation.surface: A holiday on an island begins with a cold welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is the large Mediterranean island off the toe of Italy.

clue.text: Momentum and energy introduced by politician in woven suit

indicators.note: woven threads are interlaced, so the letters are worked into a new pattern
in places these letters inside the other piece

explanation.surface: An MP in a tweed suit brings drive and energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or driving push that keeps something moving, much like momentum.

clue.text: Former pupil facing college surrounded by outworn barrier

indicators.note: something surrounded by another is enclosed within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil
stale means worn out, no longer fresh
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: An old boy confronts his tired college, a barrier to progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy' (OB) is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is anything in the way that blocks progress, much as a barrier does.

clue.text: Sloth by lieutenant keeping people in disorder

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the next piece is held inside

blocks.note: the ai is a three-toed sloth

explanation.surface: Laziness from an officer leaves the troops in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like laziness; it is the animal, the ai.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is an illness, and a disorder in medical use means a malady.

clue.text: One not to be seen supplying pop?

definitions.text: One not to be seen supplying pop?

blocks.clueFragment: One not to be seen supplying pop?
blocks.note: surface: an invisible supplier of fizzy drinks
setter's reading: pop is a gunshot, fired by a hidden marksman

explanation.walkthrough: Pop as soda leads to a drinks supplier; pop as the crack of a gun leads to a concealed shooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman who shoots from a concealed position, so stays unseen.

clue.text: Hold off recall of outcast

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word comes back the other way

blocks.note: a leper is a social outcast

explanation.surface: Fend off the return of someone shunned by society.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to drive back or ward off an attacker, which is to hold them off.

clue.text: Feudal superior getting complete praise when mentioned

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the words count by their sound

explanation.surface: A feudal lord receives full praise whenever his name comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech laud and lord sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An overlord was a ruler above other lords in the feudal hierarchy.

clue.text: Leave foreign capital without ring

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: Quito is the capital of Ecuador
O is round like a ring; it is removed

explanation.surface: Depart from an overseas capital without your wedding ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a place is to depart from it, a verb synonym of leave.

clue.text: Weapon that's leaking, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the answer goes by its sound

explanation.surface: A gun that is leaking, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: The Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Spade, say, endlessly varied type for moving earth

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is lost
letters that are moving shift position, so they settle in a new order

blocks.note: the word missing its last letter
E is the abbreviation for earth

explanation.surface: A spade is a tool for shifting soil, and comes in many kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: Spade is not the garden tool but Sam Spade, Dashiell Hammett's detective in The Maltese Falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Spade is a hard-boiled fictional detective, an example of a private investigator.

clue.text: Cruise, perhaps, miles off circling island

indicators.note: something off is out of its proper state, so these letters are disordered
circling means going around, so these letters wrap around another piece

blocks.note: Is. is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A cruise ship sails some miles offshore, going round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruise is not a holiday voyage but the cruise missile.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise missile is a guided weapon, so Cruise is an example of a missile.

clue.text: Come to a decision about a coastal city

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the other

explanation.surface: Choosing whether to move to a city by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a port city in Washington state on Puget Sound, on the Pacific coast.
